correctness.rationale: At most one omitted private vertex per K_r twin class is forced by location; complementary domination requires a member of T in every hub-plus-clique cluster. The exhaustive three local options are: selected hub and one omitted private; omitted hub and all selected private; omitted hub and one omitted private, the last iff an adjacent hub is selected. Each outside signature contains a nonempty cluster-private subset since r>=2, so different clusters cannot collide. Inside the third type, selected adjacent hub separates the two outsiders. This is a genuine necessity-and-sufficiency proof, not an empirical pattern. The binomial product counts exactly and once. For c(A)=|N_H(A)\A|, D=A union (V\N_H[A]) dominates and has n-c(A) vertices; a minimum dominating A attains max c=n-gamma(H), proving the extreme exponent and coefficient. Independently reconstructed direct-definition enumeration for all 75 labelled H of order 1..4 and r=2 confirms the polynomial. The inspected repository verifier is separate and documents 90 profiles; no infinite inference is made from them.

value.rationale: A natural clique-corona operation over an arbitrary base graph exposes an exactly classified mixed-role partition family. The polynomial counts every labelled configuration, all extremizers and the host domination number, going materially beyond the recent existence theorem. The classification remains useful even for disconnected and isolate-bearing bases and is not a tiny finite case or mere renaming.

final_claim: For every nonempty labelled finite simple H (including isolated hubs), r>=2, the complete role-ordered locating-dominating/dominating complementary-partition polynomial is sum_{A subset V(H)} sum_{j=0}^{|N(A)\A|} binomial(c,j)r^{|A|+j}z^{rn-j}; min |S|=(r-1)n+gamma(H) and the extremal coefficient is explicit.
limitations: H is finite simple nonempty; r>=2; all vertices labelled, roles specified; count is potentially exponential and not a polynomial-time algorithm; finite tests do not prove unrestricted theorem.
